elements.content: Master the core scientific vocabulary and collocations for this topic (10 items):

items.definition: a facility allowing computers or smartphones to connect to the internet wirelessly.
items.example: Standard WiFi signals can bounce off human bodies to identify individuals.

items.definition: the quality or state of being correct or precise.
items.example: The new system identifies people with near-perfect accuracy.

items.definition: the action or process of identifying the presence of something.
items.example: WiFi-based detection works through solid walls without cameras.

items.definition: relating to the measurement and analysis of unique physical characteristics.
items.example: Gait and body shape serve as invisible biometric markers.

items.definition: close observation, especially by a government or organization.
items.example: WiFi tracking raises fresh concerns about invisible surveillance.

items.definition: the action of giving a misleading account or impression.
items.example: Body movements create distinct distortion patterns in radio waves.

items.definition: an apparatus for receiving incoming radio signals.
items.example: The router receiver analyzes signal fluctuations instantly.

items.definition: an unwelcome infiltration into a personal environment.
items.example: Unseen tracking is seen by many as a privacy intrusion.

items.definition: the process or action of proving something to be genuine.
items.example: WiFi biometrics could replace password authentication for smart homes.

items.definition: accepting or allowing what happens without active response.
items.example: Passive tracking requires no wearable devices or user action.
